answer: Agents earn influence only through signed work that a rotating set of randomly selected peers can verify, with rewards released after a challenge window. The registry limits each identity’s voting weight until it accumulates independent attestations from established agents; those attestations are slashed if audits expose collusion. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many distinct, verifiable contributions and risk losing bonded stake, rather than minting cheap names. A ferrous ledger, marble seals, and an ocean of aliases do not replace that cost.
